features.title: Complete embedding/retrieval lifecycle
features.value: Persisted data becomes searchable without manually creating completion records.
features.reuse: P04/14B–14D, shared provider/effect/material authorities, and the existing worker. Do not reimplement accepted components; the later 14E acceptance is recorded in current status.
deliverables: Complete delivery binding/publication and the remaining P04 rebuild/query paths under separately accepted contracts, reusing the subsequently accepted 14E implementation.
Wire production worker composition; distinguish ResultPrepared, Live, a ready generation, and a successful job.
Do not enable context/import readiness through a legacy embedding bypass.
acceptance: The real API/worker completes the permitted lifecycle against PostgreSQL under the runtime role.
Process death before/after publication leaves one canonical result and no repeated external dispatch.
Sources and queries use exact spaces/generations; partial publication and stale attempts are rejected.
features.non_goals: A new embedding model, a new queue, or administrator-assigned Succeeded state.

features.title: Shared content access and authority
features.value: New library, history, context, and export surfaces do not bypass existing restrictions.
features.reuse: Bearer identity, route inventory, capability boundaries, workspace RLS, and existing classification/share checks.
deliverables: Define a read/disclosure/write operation matrix for HTTP, MCP, UI, and worker.
Check current permissions and the exact revision before new read paths disclose content.
Reject imported actor/workspace/grants; exclude secrets and denied content from errors, search snippets, and logs.
acceptance: Unrelated workspaces/principals receive no protected bytes, source names, or object-existence leaks through response side channels.
Revocation blocks the next read/download even when a previous cache/idempotency receipt exists.
Unknown routes and missing policy fail explicitly; test direct database writes under the restricted runtime role.
features.non_goals: SSO/federation or a new policy engine.

features.title: Atomic memory writes and durable replay
features.value: Lost HTTP responses or outbox failures neither create duplicate memory nor leave changes without audit.
features.reuse: Existing CAS, save_memory_with_revision, GovernedMutationRepository::commit_in, and participant save_in methods.
deliverables: Commit revision/source/search projection, audit, outbox, and the accepted-request receipt in one unit of work.
Exclude newly allocated UUIDs from semantic request identity; bind the result to actor, operation, and scope.
Move all writers in the selected memory scope to the common boundary; do not retain a legacy bypass.
acceptance: Audit/outbox/receipt failure rolls back the canonical mutation.
Identical concurrent requests converge on the same IDs; the same key with different semantics conflicts.
Stale versions cannot lose newer changes; replay cannot disclose content denied after the original request.
features.non_goals: Rewriting the general runtime or removing existing CAS protection.

features.title: Reproducible setup and a safe Console
features.value: Engineers can diagnose setup without guessing bootstrap-key or authentication details.
features.reuse: Compose provisioning/migration/init services, mounted secret store, nginx token proxy, and startup checks.
deliverables: Document and test one supported bootstrap/role-provisioning path without embedding keys in images.
Align Vite development and container authentication; never put credentials in a VITE_* bundle.
Separate liveness, database/schema readiness, and feature readiness; persist every required vault volume.
acceptance: A clean isolated environment with authorized preprovisioned secrets starts using the published procedure.
Empty secret stores, overlapping roots, and invalid policy settings fail clearly.
Console's proxy is not exposed as a general administrative endpoint; invalid credentials cannot grant access.
features.non_goals: A cloud installer, automatic production-secret generation, or login UX substituting for a real security boundary.

features.title: Backup, restore, and populated-installation upgrades
features.value: Users retain long-term memory across upgrades, restart, and recovery.
features.reuse: P05, existing migration checks, installation permit/fingerprint, and material authorities.
deliverables: Qualify a consistent database/WAL backup procedure with mandatory vault dependencies.
Test upgrade with existing revisions/receipts and an approved freeze/drain mode.
Distinguish database backup, knowledge export, and full installation recovery; do not promise an untested downgrade.
acceptance: Restore into a separate environment and compare selected canonical IDs, history, permissions, and material availability.
A missing key or incompatible migration checksum is not replaced by a new empty installation.
Cover failure at freeze, copy, activation, and restart boundaries, not only the backup command's exit code.
features.non_goals: An independent restore runtime or fictional successful qualification of a restored journal.

features.title: Executable checks and manageable CI cost
features.value: Regression feedback is timely without omitting entire test categories.
features.reuse: Existing Rust/Node/Compose CI and scope/protocol checks.
deliverables: Separate fast, PostgreSQL, composition/fault, and release suites; add an explicit doctest step.
Measure disk, RAM, and build duration before changing profiles or test-target layout.
Test through ordinary product entry points; setup failure is not behavioral RED.
acceptance: A control doctest/compile_fail case is actually executed by the selected command.
Runtime-role regression checks detect violations without administrative privileges.
CI changes preserve risk-class coverage; green jobs are not obtained by disabling expensive checks.
features.non_goals: Splitting crates by arbitrary line counts or cutting tests to obtain a green badge.

features.title: Accurate progress and diagnostics
features.value: Operators distinguish queues, blockers, and unknown outcomes from successful execution.
features.reuse: worker --once, outbox attempts/dead-letter, canonical Run projections, health, and audit.
deliverables: Show the expected dependency, a safe stop reason, and the permitted next step.
Separate accepted/applied/indexed from process exit and Run outcome.
Keep content, tokens, and unjustified protected-object counts out of metrics.
acceptance: Bounded worker outcomes 0/3/1 describe a cycle result, not overall qualification.
An unhandled topic stays pending and visible to operators; restart does not erase the failure reason.
After reconnect, the UI reads persisted state rather than optimistic local success.
features.non_goals: Automatic retry of every UNKNOWN outcome.

features.title: Governed content, retention, and erasure
features.value: Import and export do not create unmanaged sensitive-content copies.
features.reuse: MaterialIntentCommands, vault, erasure/blockers, and existing export/purge policy contracts.
deliverables: Allow source staging/download only through lawful material-owner/read paths.
Define preview/export/context-evidence retention and its relationship to source retention.
Do not replace policy-driven erasure with moving a record to trash or retaining plaintext in audit.
acceptance: Prepared material cannot be read as Live; revoked access blocks subsequent downloads.
Cancelled/failed import leaves no accessible unowned staging data.
Erasure checks include managed copies and explicitly exclude any promise to recall external exports.
features.non_goals: A new vault, plaintext temporary-file fallback, or destruction of original audit facts.

features.title: Useful Memory reads, library, and history
features.value: Users can inspect content and the exact revision before editing or using it.
features.reuse: MemoryUseCases/find_revision, PgRevisionHydrator, current MemoryResponse, and MCP get_memory.
deliverables: Implement one authorized query port for detail, history, and browse.
Preserve legacy DTO compatibility or explicitly version the change; do not describe new routes as existing ones.
Bind pages/cursors to filters, scope, and snapshot; never replace a historical revision with current content.
acceptance: One call returns authorized content, revision number, and safe provenance references.
History opens exact revisions and cannot be bypassed using another memory's ID.
Browse avoids browser-side N+1 requests and protected-record leaks through totals/cursors.
features.non_goals: Changing lifecycle, widening access, or adding another memory store.

features.title: Rendered Context API with explicit budget guarantees
features.value: Clients receive usable model context rather than section counters.
features.reuse: RetrievalService, ContextPackBuilder, existing temporal/intent fields, and generation guards.
deliverables: Return actual sections/rendered content, exact revisions, warnings, and disclosure destination.
Distinguish byte-only limits from hard-token bounds using a qualified tokenizer.
Do not replace missing content with explanation text; bound the complete rendered payload.
acceptance: Returned text matches permitted revisions; sources are not elevated into instructions.
UTF-8/tokenizer accounting matches the final context, including separators.
Stale generations or missing policy do not become empty successful responses.
features.non_goals: A new retrieval engine or an unverified universal token estimator.

features.title: Corrections and restoration of earlier text
features.value: Users correct memory without destroying history or other writers' changes.
features.reuse: revise_memory, immutable revisions, existing CAS, and the MW atomic writer.
deliverables: Require explicit correction reasons and current-state preconditions.
Restore creates a new revision with provenance for the operation.
Do not hide label transitions inside ordinary edits; preserve the current classification-change refusal.
acceptance: Concurrent editing returns a conflict without silent overwrite.
Replaying a correction/restore returns the same receipt.
Earlier revisions remain immutable; new source facts record the author's action rather than fabricated confirmation.
features.non_goals: Irreversible purge disguised as ordinary deletion, automatic semantic merge, or automatic confidence elevation.

features.title: Memory Console: search, detail, and editing
features.value: Memory management requires neither SQL, handcrafted JSON, nor knowledge of the internal graph.
features.reuse: MemoryConsole.tsx, existing design system, typed HTTP client, and ErrorBoundary.
deliverables: Wire real library/detail/history routes and correction/restore actions.
Show sources, timestamps, revision conflicts, and persisted state after restart.
Separate empty/loading/denied/unavailable/degraded; new controls must not simulate missing functionality.
acceptance: A browser → HTTP → PostgreSQL edit survives reload and is visible from another client.
Two editors expose the correct conflict and preserve drafts until resolution.
Keyboard navigation, focus/error announcements, and distinguishable states pass the browser checklist.
features.non_goals: A complete redesign, 3D graph explorer, or separate Console.

features.title: Bounded source import with preview
features.value: Users can populate memory from an existing documentation folder without requiring an LLM.
features.reuse: MW source/collection design and existing memory/event/material/worker boundaries.
deliverables: Support Markdown, TXT, and the defined JSON format; the local scanner reads only the selected directory, never arbitrary server paths.
Pin exact bytes, policy, and parser version in preview; Apply operates on that snapshot.
Separate source identity from hashes and file paths; expose individual item refusals.
acceptance: A file changed after preview cannot be applied under earlier confirmation.
Identical input replay creates no new canonical revisions; a distinct source with identical bytes remains distinct.
Reject traversal, symlink escape, BOM, invalid UTF-8, oversized input, and duplicate IDs before mutation.
features.non_goals: Default LLM extraction, PDF/OCR, remote crawling, or access to the server's general filesystem.

features.title: Synchronization that preserves editorial changes
features.value: Document updates do not destroy corrections accepted by the user.
features.reuse: MW B/I/M decision contract, source/revision identities, and the shared atomic writer.
deliverables: Retain base imported content B, incoming source I, and current memory M.
Create domain sync conflicts for divergent changes; explicit resolution requires preconditions.
Missing does not mean deletion; renames require stable identity or explicit mapping.
acceptance: Keep-local, accept-source, and manual-merge produce the documented revision/receipt outcome; keep_manual may retain the existing revision as specified by MW.
Cancellation racing Apply does not promise rollback of committed items; show applied and pending subsets.
Failure after item commit and before acknowledgement does not duplicate source versions or revisions.
features.non_goals: Unrestricted LLM conflict resolution or last-modified-wins.

features.title: Portable knowledge export and import
features.value: Users can take their permitted data and reproduce an experiment in another installation.
features.reuse: MW portable schema, material/download policy, and source/memory identities.
deliverables: Produce versioned JSON with permitted history and references; Markdown is a reading view.
Assign new local IDs in the receiving installation and treat remote history as an external source.
Separate knowledge export from runtime backup; omission descriptions cannot disclose denied data.
acceptance: Round-trip permitted content/provenance without transferring grants, secrets, or qualification.
Reject dangling references, future formats, imported authority, and invalid active revisions.
Revocation before a subsequent download blocks disclosure; a previously delivered copy is not automatically recalled.
features.non_goals: Full installation recovery from knowledge JSON or guaranteed revocation of external copies.

features.title: One typed client and a stable external contract
features.value: Integrators use a small API rather than reimplementing Vestrace's internal mechanics.
features.reuse: apps/console/src/sdk/client.ts and one shared application read/write path for HTTP/MCP.
deliverables: Make Console the first complete client; use new DTOs only after their endpoints exist.
Pass idempotency/preconditions explicitly; do not convert read errors, retryability, or UNKNOWN into success.
Choose the first external SDK from an actual integrator's needs instead of publishing three at once.
acceptance: Contract fixtures pass through real HTTP; parsing rejects incompatible responses.
The client cannot assign trusted actor/workspace values or blindly retry irreversible mutations.
A fresh session against the same backend demonstrates continued work.
features.non_goals: Advertising package names or SDK methods before they exist.

features.title: Golden workflow and first-result documentation
features.value: An engineer unfamiliar with internals completes a task and understands its limitations.
features.reuse: The documentation structure, MW fixture corpus, and existing local runtime.
deliverables: Document one complete task: import documents, recall a decision, correct it, synchronize, and export.
Show normal execution alongside a fault case.
Label each command as current or proposed and state its environment prerequisites.
acceptance: Two independent testers complete the published workflow; record assistance required.
Verify expected results against the actual version; exclude sensitive output from public examples.
Do not replace unexecuted steps with demo UI or manual SQL.
features.non_goals: An unmeasured marketing promise of a five-minute setup.

features.title: Temporal knowledge: current state, as_of, and past awareness
features.value: The system distinguishes old decisions, late corrections, and information available in the past.
features.reuse: TimePerspective, revision hydration, occurrence/recording/validity contracts; do not create another timeline.
deliverables: Define validity-time and recorded-as-known semantics separately rather than treating both as as_of.
Preserve exact revision references in responses, without latest-version substitution.
Resolve storage/indexing gaps through an explicit contract before promising complete bitemporal replay.
acceptance: One corpus with a late correction produces the distinct expected current and historical answers.
Superseded knowledge is not current; retrospective reads still require current access.
Insufficient history produces an explicit knowledge boundary, not fabricated reconstruction.
features.non_goals: Treating a document date as trusted event time or inventing past knowledge.

features.title: Provenance and governed semantic conflicts
features.value: Answers can be checked against sources and disagreements resolved without hidden last-write-wins.
features.reuse: Claim/Conflict/Reconciliation domain, cognitive mutation repository, and MW correction UI.
deliverables: Distinguish byte-level sync conflicts from semantic disagreement between assertions.
Show permitted support/contradiction references and decisions; never guess revision lineage.
Add an impact view for changes without rewriting past Run context.
acceptance: Two admissible contradictory sources remain explicit until lawful resolution.
Sources with different permissions cannot disclose protected facts through a public digest.
Rejected or new resolutions preserve historical basis and actor identity.
features.non_goals: Confidence percentages presented as truth probabilities or automatic trust from usage frequency.

features.title: One qualified external memory integration
features.value: DSH or another selected runtime uses Vestrace knowledge across sessions.
features.reuse: MCP tools, content-read gates, one typed client, and existing authentication binding.
deliverables: Begin read-only, then add explicit remember, then separately opt-in capture.
Let the application define optional-memory and required-context policy; capture creates source-attributed observations.
Pin client versions and one cross-session scenario; connecting memory does not govern all other runtime effects.
acceptance: A new session receives accepted corrections; another identity receives no protected record.
Unavailable memory follows a documented failure mode rather than silently changing the prompt.
Capture replay does not duplicate knowledge; model output does not automatically become confirmed fact.
features.non_goals: Claimed partnerships, governance of every external-runtime tool, or every integration at once.

features.title: Measured memory quality and regressions
features.value: Added memory complexity is justified by task outcomes, not the number of new tests.
features.reuse: Raw evaluation facts separate from learned projections, MW acceptance, and synthetic sources.
deliverables: Build a versioned corpus for currency, contradictions, missing information, permissions, erasure, and multiple sessions.
Compare with a simple full-text-search baseline using identical data, model, and token budget.
Measure retrieval evidence separately from answer quality; do not delegate ACL gates to a model judge.
acceptance: Every case identifies expected permitted source IDs and forbidden conclusions.
Tokenizer, model, or retrieval-setting changes create a new experiment rather than rewrite old results.
A hard-safety regression blocks publication even when average quality improves.
features.non_goals: A universal quality percentage, market proof from stars, or model judging as a security oracle.

features.title: Context inspector and decision explanations
features.value: Engineers can explain why an answer used particular knowledge and why a new version changed the result.
features.reuse: Retrieval journals, exact revision references, ModelRequestEvidence, and audit/read gates.
deliverables: Show the permitted query/filter/candidates/sections/rendered-payload chain.
Distinguish issued context, client acknowledgement, and independently observed model requests.
Bound trace retention and access; context must not become a permanent hidden copy of erased knowledge.
acceptance: Comparing configurations exposes changed source revisions and reasons.
Unauthorized users cannot obtain candidates through debug endpoints.
Missing request observation is explicit; a stored payload is not proof of model use.
features.non_goals: A promise of complete deterministic LLM-output replay.

features.title: Background consolidation and updatable digests
features.value: A new task can begin with a short current digest and verifiable sources.
features.reuse: Memory revisions, derivation, existing execution/outbox, and learned projections; no independent reflection runtime.
deliverables: Start with one digest type: project decisions, constraints, and open questions.
Record source revisions, method/model revision, validity watermark, and stale state.
Source changes invalidate the digest; publishing a new canonical conclusion requires a separate mutation.
acceptance: The digest references exact inputs and cannot acquire broader disclosure permissions than its sources.
Correction or revocation marks it stale before subsequent use.
Background failure preserves earlier canonical facts; retry converges by job/input identity.
features.non_goals: Self-modifying policy, automatic truth promotion, or many indefinite background agents.

features.title: Retrieval cost and incremental representations
features.value: Changing one source does not require pointless rebuilding of the entire corpus.
features.reuse: P04 spaces/generations, source revisions, and explicit processing recipes.
deliverables: Treat new bytes, parser recipes, and embedding models as distinct reasons for reprocessing.
Measure warm/cold latency, memory/disk use, and the number of recomputed items.
Optimize after correctness is established; do not weaken guards for benchmarks.
acceptance: Unchanged data creates neither canonical revisions nor arbitrary new provenance.
A Ready generation does not mix incompatible spaces.
Measurements use comparable hardware/data and report trade-offs rather than only the best run.
features.non_goals: A custom vector database or premature distributed deployment.

features.title: Complete providers, models, and agent Runs
features.value: Agent workflows use real configuration and preserve the selected provider identity.
features.reuse: P03 model/connection revisions, q1 qualification, ModelBindingSnapshot, and the shared provider graph.
deliverables: Complete P06 under its frozen scope, including no_auth/Bearer paths and actual models.
Do not choose providers from current environment variables instead of the accepted binding.
acceptance: Browser/HTTP creates lawful configuration; after restart, a Run retains pinned revisions.
Qualification or credential refusal prevents dispatch with safe diagnostics.
features.non_goals: Dozens of providers before one complete path is accepted.

features.title: Interaction kernel, artifacts, and retention
features.value: Messages, actions, and materials form one coherent interaction history.
features.reuse: P07 canonical Run, interaction/artifact contracts, content materials, and retention authority.
deliverables: Complete the thread/message/state/context kernel and artifact lifecycle through one Run.
Align replay low-water marks and retention without a second session source of truth.
acceptance: Restart/reconnect preserves canonical actions without duplication.
Erasure or expiry is reflected in subsequent reads/replay according to contract.
features.non_goals: A new chat runtime that bypasses Run.

features.title: Complete pinned AG-UI integration
features.value: The official client receives consistent event streaming and recovery.
features.reuse: P08, pinned protocol locks, the interaction kernel, and the existing Console.
deliverables: Use the specified endpoint and compatible client; do not develop legacy split routes into a second protocol.
Test streaming, replay, interruption, tools, and required multimodal paths within frozen scope.
acceptance: The official pinned client passes interoperability and reconnect cases.
Server events project canonical state; there is no UI-only success.
features.non_goals: Additional protocol versions without separate compatibility gates.

features.title: A2A server, client, and workflow step
features.value: Agent-to-agent exchange works without competing execution truth.
features.reuse: P09/P10, canonical Run/effects, connection qualification, and pinned SDK/specification.
deliverables: Implement server/card/six core operations under P09 first, then outbound workflow steps under P10.
Check SSRF/authentication, deadlines, cancellation, retained replay, and uncertain external outcomes.
acceptance: The official contract/TCK and an independent sample server produce recorded interoperability results.
Outbound failure is not permission to retry; a remote assertion does not increase local trust.
features.non_goals: Complete federation or trust in self-signed cards without policy.

features.title: Remaining Console workflows
features.value: The approved menu contains no enabled stubs or settings with no effect.
features.reuse: P11 pages, settings, workflows, triggers, evaluations, audit, and the existing SDK.
deliverables: Complete the eleven-menu workflows from the frozen program; distinguish read views from applied settings.
Reuse memory read/write APIs rather than duplicate their behavior in another page.
acceptance: Browser scenarios and restart cover every enabled function.
Keep 501/disabled states honest until implementation; enabled settings change observable runtime behavior.
features.non_goals: A separate no-code editor product.

features.title: Full v1.0 qualification and compatibility
features.value: A release represents a specific verified promise rather than the existence of files.
features.reuse: P12, Accepted specifications, qualification evidence, and source/image/config/model/protocol identities.
deliverables: Approve the exact shipping manifest, supported environment, and contract freeze.
Qualify included MW features separately and explicitly add them to the release matrix.
Do not relabel a narrower alpha as the full frozen v1.0 release.
acceptance: Every required P12 evidence source is fresh and belongs to the same target identities.
Skipped/blocked checks are not PASS; release notes disclose limitations and migration policy.
features.non_goals: Defining v1.0 by a calendar date or line count.

features.title: Team memory and expanded federation
features.value: Teams can safely use shared knowledge under explicit conditions.
features.reuse: Existing capabilities, share grants, mounts, and Brain–Face–Organ boundaries.
deliverables: Validate demand and tenancy first; then define shared scope, identity lifecycle, SSO/admission, and reviewed sharing.
Do not interpret local single-workspace v1 as a promise of ready enterprise federation.
acceptance: Independent real principals/tenants and revocation pass an adversarial matrix.
A pilot measures administrative cost; neither global namespace nor mounts imply trust.
features.non_goals: Silently widening the supported deployment topology.

features.title: Managed deployment and multi-installation operations
features.value: Deployment and maintenance may become a service after demand is validated.
features.reuse: Installer, restore, telemetry, identity, and release qualification rather than a new semantic model.
deliverables: Decide after measured self-hosted pilots; define SLA/SLO, upgrade/cost model, and incident ownership.
Separate management-plane and data-plane authority; billing does not grant memory access.
acceptance: A pilot measures restore/upgrade without undocumented author intervention.
Control-plane failure does not rewrite canonical state; test tenant isolation on the chosen topology.
features.non_goals: Launching SaaS before data preservation is verified.

features.title: Additional SDKs, connectors, and formats
features.value: Expand access only for demonstrated user tasks.
features.reuse: The first SDK, bounded importer, existing disclosure policy, and source identity.
deliverables: Choose each next language/connector pair from a reproducible user requirement.
Review extraction, retention, and network threat models separately for PDF, media, or cloud sources.
acceptance: New adapters pass the same contract suite without changing authority semantics.
Each adapter has a support owner and versioned fixtures; no hidden external calls occur.
features.non_goals: A catalog of dozens of unsupported integrations.

features.title: Portable development harness
features.value: Reuse the development method after collecting evidence of its value.
features.reuse: Frozen scope, persistent builder, independent review, evidence, and mutation tests.
deliverables: Measure escaped defects, review cost, reproducibility, and portability; improve the harness for Vestrace first.
Extract a separate tool only with independent demand and a dedicated owner.
acceptance: Another small repository reproduces a bounded workflow without E:/ or undocumented local assumptions.
Measurements include both detected and missed defects, not just review counts.
features.non_goals: A second large product before external adoption of Vestrace.

editorial_note: Original roadmap source pins and dependency graph are preserved. Current status records the later Task 14E acceptance and occupied migration 0196. No runtime tests were run in this refactor.
